chapter: Le Ruban Bleu, retirement and community work
title: Practicing trombone and losing the trumpet
summary: She practiced valve trombone, and recently lost her pocket trumpet from a car while on a gig.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Cornet or trumpet: choosing and owning horns

blocks.x: So you did a few appearances then after '56?

Yeah, with a group that was going to go someplace and do something. I remember going out on a gig with J. C. Higginbotham, and PeeWee Russell, and Buck Clayton and some other guys, and I was - I didn't have a hard case for my horn, I just had a cloth case made for it. And my valve trombone wound up on the bottom of the rest of the instruments and boy was it mangled all up. So I thought they was just trying to put me out of business. I was getting too good for them. But I finally gave it away later to a young man, a young blind piano

player who is now out in Ohio. But I practiced quite a bit on that trombone, and after I gave that horn away I got a flu-horn and I've been practicing on that. Right now of course, Bill Ratzenberg gave me that little pocket trumpet.
No, you told me last time to jump ahead a little bit, you told me last time that you had lost that trumpet.

I have and I haven't found it either. And I got a call from Bill Ratzenberg, he's putting music into an old club up there, a country club, and he's putting together packages now and he called me up. I'm supposed to go up there and he said to be sure and bring your horn. I don't know, I haven't broken the news to him yet that I haven't got the horn. I don't know whether I should break the news to him and let him give me another one or go out and try to find a replacement. I'm weighing that situation.
Well I was doing a gig with Dill Jones out in West Hampton and I drove out to Port Washington where Dill lives . . .

Just to make it clear, this is about how long now?

About three months ago. And before that has a very large parking lot and I've worked there with Dill there's a library in Port Washington and he said that I would drive the car there and drive my car there and park it, transfer to his car and we would go out to West Hampton. Well I had my horn with me, in fact, I played it a little bit out in West Hampton and we came back and transferring me and my music and the horn into my car, I'll put the horn on top of my car and I didn't know it. I drove home and when I got home I didn't find the horn in the car. So I called Dill and asked him if it was still in his car and he told me that he had placed it on the top of my car. So somewhere along the way it fell off. I don't know whether it might have got run over by a truck or whether somebody found it. We've tried to locate it but to no avail up to this point.
